class_name: 話題-尊敬-ニオカレマシテハ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: A rare, old-fashioned use of には that marks an esteemed person as the topic where modern Japanese would use が or は, surviving mainly in set letter openings (先生にはご健勝のことと存じます) and in period fiction. Learners should recognize it rather than produce it; におかれましては is the living equivalent, and ordinary には (location, purpose, comparison) is an unrelated everyday combination of に and は.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]にはお変[か]わりなくお過[す]ごしのことと存[ぞん]じます。
examples.english: I trust that you, sir, are keeping as well as ever.

examples.ruby: 陛下[へいか]には本日[ほんじつ]ご出発[しゅっぱつ]の予定[よてい]でございます。
examples.english: His Majesty is scheduled to depart today.

examples.ruby: 殿[との]にはたいそうご機嫌[きげん]がよろしいご様子[ようす]だ。
examples.english: His lordship appears to be in exceedingly good humor.

glosses: in your case; I trust that you
patterns.usage_note: The honorific dressing-up of においては, used to raise a respected addressee to topic in business letters, invitations and formal notices, most often in the opening health-and-prosperity greeting. Style guides state that it takes a person or an organization only, not a thing, so 御社の商品におかれましては is treated as an error; におかれては is the slightly lighter variant. It is written-register through and through; archaic honorific には fills the same role in classical and epistolary Japanese, but におかれましては is built on においては, not derived from には.

examples.ruby: 貴社[きしゃ]におかれましては、益々[ますます]ご発展[はってん]のこととお慶[よろこ]び申[もう]し上[あ]げます。
examples.english: We are delighted to hear of your company's continued growth.

examples.ruby: 読者[どくしゃ]におかれましては、ご不便[ふべん]をおかけし申[もう]し訳[わけ]ございません。
examples.english: We apologize to our readers for the inconvenience this has caused.

examples.ruby: 会員[かいいん]におかれては、期日[きじつ]までにご登録[とうろく]をお願[ねが]いします。
examples.english: Members are asked to complete their registration by the deadline.
